title: Incinerator
model_title: Rotary Kiln Incinerator with Secondary Combustion Chamber

introduction.definition: A rotary kiln incinerator burns solid, sludge and liquid wastes. The waste, fed at the upper end, tumbles down the slowly rotating, slightly inclined kiln as it dries, burns and becomes ash. The gases pass to a secondary combustion chamber where an afterburner completes combustion before heat recovery, quenching and gas cleaning.
key_points: Kiln rotation tumbles and mixes waste
SCC: ≥ 850 °C for ≥ 2 s (EU IED; 1100 °C for > 1 % halogens)

temperature.title: Secondary chamber: temperature and residence time
temperature.description: Solids burn and ash out in the kiln (often ~ 850–1200 °C). Gases are then held in the secondary chamber; EU rules (Industrial Emissions Directive) require at least 850 °C for 2 s (1100 °C if the waste contains more than 1 % halogenated organics as chlorine) to complete combustion of organic compounds. Rapid quenching afterwards limits dioxin re-formation.

video_tutorials.title: Incinerator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Incinerator.
A rotary kiln incinerator burns solid, sludge and liquid wastes.
The waste, fed at the upper end, tumbles down the slowly rotating, slightly inclined kiln as it dries, burns and becomes ash.
The gases pass to a secondary combustion chamber where an afterburner completes combustion before heat recovery, quenching and gas cleaning.
Typical applications include hazardous and clinical waste; industrial and chemical wastes; contaminated soils.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Rotary Kiln: Shell, Refractory, Riding Tyres & Girth Gear (inclined, rotating), Feed-End Hood, Waste Feed Chute (ram) & Primary Burner, Secondary Combustion Chamber (≥ 850 °C, ≥ 2 s) & Ash Quench below, Hot Gas Outlet to Boiler / Quench & Air Pollution Control.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Incinerator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Incinerator.
Monitor SCC temperature, CO, O₂ and shell temperatures.
Inspect tyres, rollers, seals.
Reline refractory; replace seals.
Watch for refractory failure: shell hot spots. Common cause: thermal shock, slag attack.
Watch for low SCC temperature: emission limit breach risk. Common cause: afterburner fault, wet waste.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
